served.stem: The passage explains that an arbuscular fungus has never been grown to completion on a plate without a plant because the fungus
choices: can store lipid only while it is attached to a living root
loses the ability to take up phosphate when no root is present
needs a mantle of root tissue in order to produce its spores
cannot make fatty acids and must be handed them
depends on carbon dioxide that living roots release into soil
served.bankWhy: Paragraph 7 calls lipid the more surprising half of the bill. Arbuscular fungi cannot manufacture their own fatty acids, and that dependence is given as a large part of why they cannot be raised to completion without a host.

proof.quote: cannot manufacture their own fatty acids and must be handed them by a host

passage.title: The Trade Beneath the Forest Floor

distractorNotes: Paragraph 3 mentions vesicles storing lipid but never makes storage itself conditional on a living root.
Phosphate uptake is the fungus's own job in paragraph 6, and nothing ties it to the presence of a root.
Mantles belong to the ectomycorrhizal type in paragraph 4, and the passage never links them to spore production.
Soil carbon dioxide appears in paragraph 12 as a route a label can take, not as something a fungus must be fed.

answer.text: cannot make fatty acids and must be handed them
answer.line: Paragraph 7: arbuscular fungi cannot make their own fatty acids and must be handed them by a host. That is largely why.

steps: Read the start of that sentence. They "cannot manufacture their own fatty acids and must be handed them by a host."
The word which ties that gap to the plate result. The gap is making, not storing.

choices.text: can store lipid only while it is attached to a living root
choices.note: Vesicles store lipid, paragraph 3, but storage is not the problem. The gap is making fatty acids at all.

choices.text: loses the ability to take up phosphate when no root is present
choices.note: Phosphate is what travels back above all, so a phosphate reason sounds right, but nothing ties its uptake to a root being present.

choices.text: needs a mantle of root tissue in order to produce its spores
choices.note: A mantle belongs to the other partnership, paragraph 4, and it is fungal tissue, not root tissue. Spores appear only in paragraph 13.

choices.text: cannot make fatty acids and must be handed them
choices.note: Sentence 4: cannot manufacture their own fatty acids and must be handed them by a host.

choices.text: depends on carbon dioxide that living roots release into soil
choices.note: Respired carbon dioxide is in paragraph 12, as a route a label can take. It is never something a fungus must be fed.
